What to plant in Cross River State

Quick answer: Cross River State is in Nigeria's South-South (Humid rainforest). The rainy season runs March – November (two peaks). Its best-known crops are african yam bean, cassava, white yam, water yam, cocoyam (taro) and fluted pumpkin (ugu). Plant rain-fed crops only after the rains have truly started.

RegionSouth-South
Rainy seasonMarch – November (two peaks)
VegetationHumid rainforest
Capital (weather point)Calabar

Questions farmers in Cross River ask

What crops grow best in Cross River State?

African yam bean, Cassava, White yam, Water yam, Cocoyam (Taro), Fluted pumpkin (Ugu), Waterleaf, Pineapple, Plantain, Banana, African pear (Ube), Avocado, Coconut, Cocoa, Oil palm, Rubber, Coffee (Robusta), Tannia (New cocoyam), Uziza and Bitter kola are among the best-known crops of Cross River State.

When does the rainy season start in Cross River State?

The rainy season in Cross River State usually runs March – November (two peaks). The rains have truly started when about 20 mm of rain falls within 3 days. Use our live check before you plant.

What can I plant in Cross River State in the dry season?

With irrigation or on fadama (wet valley) land: rice, white yam, tomato and cucumber.

What should I plant in Cross River State at the start of the rains?

maize, african yam bean, cassava, white yam, water yam, cocoyam (taro), sweet potato and tomato are commonly planted when the rains begin.
